title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Onboarding, Quantization, Guardrails and Regression Playbook
author: Ariana Patel
body:
Summary:

This playbook consolidates the applied ML evaluation workflows used by Redwood Inference for model onboarding, prompt-set and benchmark management, quantization profile verification, quality guardrails, and regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, applied-research engineers, SREs responsible for model rollouts, and product owners who own downstream quality.

Purpose and scope:

- Ensure a repeatable, observable, and auditable path from model import to production rollout.
- Define required eval harness checks, prompt and benchmark coverage, quantization validation, and regression response procedures.
- Scope covers open-model onboarding (public weights), Redwood-verified variants (quantized/pruned), and internal rollout policies for Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Audience:

- ML Engineers, Applied Research, Model Infra, SRE, Product Owners.

Roles and responsibilities:

| Role | Team | Responsibilities |
|------|------|------------------|
| Model Owner | Applied ML / Engineering | Lead onboarding PR, maintain prompt sets, respond to regression tickets. |
| Eval Owner | Applied ML / Evals | Author harness tests, maintain CI, provide pass/fail criteria. |
| Quantization Owner | Eng-serving-runtime | Maintain quant profiles, run quantization CI, verify kernel parity. |
| Rollout Owner | Eng-platform / SRE | Coordinate canary/A-B, monitor SLOs and cost metrics, execute rollback. |

Key definitions and signals:

- Regression: any statistically significant (p < 0.05) deterioration on a pre-defined metric or prompt set compared to the pinned baseline.
- Async KPIs: latency P99, tail token generation time, per-token inference cost, hallucination rate (as defined per task).
- Guardrail thresholds (defaults):
  - Latency P95 increase > 15% vs baseline -> investigate
  - Latency P99 increase > 20% -> pause rollout
  - Accuracy/Task-specific metric drop > 2% absolute (or 5% relative) -> trigger triage
  - Hallucination rate increase > 3 percentage points -> investigate

End-to-end onboarding workflow (high-level):

1. Model intake and metadata validation
   - Create onboarding PR with model metadata: architecture, tokenizer, expected sequence lengths, training data license, FLOPs estimate, baseline evaluation run id.
   - Attach model checkpoint storage location and checksum.
2. Local compatibility checks (CI)
   - Tokenizer sanity (round-trip tests)
   - Forward/backward pass smoke (per-device) to ensure layer shapes and dtype compatibility.
3. Eval-harness baseline run (must pass before quantization starts)
   - Run the eval harness against the canonical prompt-set: small, medium, and stress suites.
   - Produce: metric table, per-prompt failure log, sampling seeds, and full output archive.
4. Quantization and optimized variant generation
   - Generate quantized variants per quantization-profiles matrix.
   - Run parity checks (see Quantization Validation below).
5. Canary and A/B rollout (staged)
   - Progressive rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with minimum 24-hour observation windows and automated gates.

Eval harness requirements and tests:

- Harness must support deterministic and stochastic modes (seeded sampling).
- Test categories: functional correctness, instruction-following, safety, hallucination detection, response grounding, and latency/cost microbenchmarks.
- Required outputs for each run: pass/fail per-test, aggregated metrics CSV, per-example outputs (.jsonl), and artifact link (S3 path).
- CI integration: All onboarding PRs must run the harness in a low-cost CI tier; a full baseline run is required on dedicated evaluation infra with GPU capacity prior to canary.

Prompt sets and benchmark hygiene:

- Prompt set taxonomy:
  - Core prompts: canonical tasks representative of customers (50–200 examples).
  - Stress prompts: long-context, multi-turn, heavy tokenization variance (100 examples).
  - Edge-case prompts: adversarial and low-resource conditions (50–100 examples).
- Authoring guidelines:
  - Each prompt must include: intent, expected labels/outputs, tolerance criteria, and owner.
  - Avoid proprietary customer data in standard prompt sets - use synthetic or scrubbed examples.
- Versioning:
  - Prompt sets are versioned in the eval-harness repository and linked by commit SHA in onboarding PRs.

Quality guardrails and metrics specification:

- Standard metrics to compute per-task: Exact Match (EM), ROUGE/L, BLEU (where applicable), F1, Response Hallucination Rate, Toxicity score (Perspective API or internal), Latency (P50/P95/P99), Cost-per-1k-tokens.
- Example guardrail table:

| Metric | Baseline | Action threshold | Automated action | Owner |
|--------|----------|------------------:|------------------|-------|
| Latency P99 | 400ms | +20% | Pause rollout, alert SRE | Rollout Owner |
| Hallucination rate | 2.1% | +3pp | Create regression ticket, tag model owner | Applied ML |
| Instruction following (hit-rate) | 92% | -2pp | Fail canary, escalate to model owner | Eval Owner |

Quantization profiles and validation matrix:

- Profiles: FP16 baseline, INT8 (symmetric/asymmetric), mixed-precision (e.g. GPTQ-style), and aggressive 4-bit variants.
- For each profile run the following matrix:
  - Functional parity (prompt-set pass/fail)
  - Metric delta (EM/F1/Task-specific) vs FP16 baseline
  - Latency and cost delta (tokens/sec, $/1M tokens)
  - Memory and peak GPU utilization
- Acceptance criteria for quant variant:
  - No metric drop > 2% absolute on core prompts OR documented fallbacks for high-risk prompts.
  - Latency improvement > 10% OR cost reduction > 15% for consideration.
  - If aggressive quantization causes targeted regressions, maintain a fallback routing policy (model variant or hosted fallback).

Regression triage playbook (on-call steps):

1. Alerting and detection
   - Alerts originate from Canary monitors, Eval regression detector, or Customer QA. Provide alert context: model id, variant, deployment id, baseline run id, related prompt-set link.
2. Initial investigation (triage within 1 hour)
   - Confirm signal: reproduce failing prompts using the eval harness against the pinned baseline and the rolled variant.
   - Check infra signals: GPU OOMs, kernel fallbacks, increased retries, or infra degradation.
3. Classify regression type
   - Functional (semantic correctness), Performance (latency/cost), Safety (toxicity/hallucination), or Infra.
4. Remediation paths
   - Quick rollback: if SLOs exceeded or core metrics drop > action threshold, rollback to previous pinned variant and notify stakeholders.
   - Hotfix: model config change (temperature, sampling) with immediate limited canary.
   - Remediate with prompt engineering: temporary routing of affected prompts to a different model variant.
5. Postmortem and permanent fix
   - Owner creates a regression ticket with root cause, remediation, and long-term fix plan. Postmortem must be published within 7 days for high-impact regressions.

Operationalizing the playbook (checklists):

- Onboarding PR checklist (required items):
  1. Model metadata and license checked.
  2. Tokenizer tests pass.
  3. Baseline eval harness run attached (artifact link).
  4. Quantization profile run matrix attached (if applicable).
  5. Prompt-set commit SHA included.
  6. Rollout strategy defined (canary percentages and duration).
  7. SLOs and guardrails documented in PR.

- Canary monitoring dashboard (minimum panels):
  - Per-model latency (P50/P95/P99), error rate, token throughput
  - Per-prompt failure heatmap (top 20 failing prompts)
  - Cost delta vs baseline (per-minute and per-token)
  - Safety signals (toxicity/hallucination aggregates)

Examples and snippets:

- Eval harness CLI (example):
  - ./eval_harness/run --model-id redwood/gpt-small-v1 --prompts=core-v3.jsonl --seed=42 --stochastic=false --artifact-path=s3://redwood-evals/runs/2029-06-15/model-x

- Quantization run (example YAML snippet):
  - profile: int8-symmetric
    calibrate_dataset: stress-v2.jsonl
    validation_prompts: core-v3.jsonl
    acceptance_delta: 0.02

Release checklist (pre-canary):

- All required eval artifacts present and linked in PR.
- Guardrail thresholds reviewed and signed off by product.
- Rollout Owner has validated runbooks and is on-call for initial 48-hour window.
- Monitoring dashboards deployed to the model team and SRE.

Appendix and references:

- Related docs: eval-harness standards, quantization profiles matrix, prompt-sets guidelines. See related_pages list at top.
- Artifact storage policy: evaluation artifacts are kept for 90 days in S3; critical regression artifacts retained 1 year.
- Contact: applied-ml-evals@redwood.com (for process questions), oncall-ml@redwood.com (for immediate incidents).
